newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister favours state money for mosques.
newsitem.headline: French minister favours state money for mosques.

text.p: French Justice Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement said on Thursday he was in favour of using public funds to help build mosques.

Asked whether he thought public resources should be spent on the construction of mosques to prevent Islamic extremists from gaining influence, Chevenement told France 2 television: "The question may be asked in order to put Islam on an equal footing.

"Because there is room for three religions, why not four if they accept the laws of the republic, in particular the secular republic, which allows religion but also is based on the idea of open debate," he said.

Noting that Islam is France's second most widespread religion, Chevenement said that Catholics, Protestants and Jews already had many places of worship, some of which were built centuries ago with state money.

"All established religions in France have suitable places of worship: churches, temples, synagogues. That comes from the length of time they have been on French soil. Islam is much newer," Chevenement added.
He noted that the only mosque erected with state resources was the Great Mosque in Paris, built in 1923.

Islamic extremists, who were responsible for a wave of bombings in France in 1995 which left eight people dead and more than 100 injured, have won followers among the children of North African immigrants in impoverished suburbs where unemployment is rife.
